text:
jill_support: FYI customer in EU reporting intermittent 403s after we rotated their service API key an hour ago. They saw about ~1-2% errors for some pods, started immediately after rotation. Attached logs: 'auth: invalid api_key' from edge-proxy.

luke_infra: thanks. do we have the rotation job id? which path in Vault did we rewrap?

jill_support: rotation job id 2026-03-17-08-eu-482. We rotated vault://secret/data/services/acme-billing and rewrapped with kms:alias/redwood-eu. Vault logs show successful rewrap at 1773809460.

maya_eng: curious if the edge/offload proxy is caching Authorization header keyed only by the header value instead of client id. if the proxy keeps an Authorization->allow mapping in memory, and the rotated key is present in some backends but not others (gc/rollout lag), you can get 403s intermittently.

sam_ops: i checked the LB + nginx edge: there is a Varnish-like proxy in front doing auth caching with TTL 300s. we pushed the new key to vault but some app pods still read the old env var (old key) until restart. that mismatch could trigger the proxy to cache a revoked key mapping.

katie_csm: customer says they did not restart their sidecar pods, they rely on envvars from our deployment that should have hot-reloaded. they reported that a manual pod restart fixed the error for that pod.

luke_infra: ok that matches. two potential contributors: 1) sidecar/env var hot reload did not pick up the new key (kube-downward/sidecar cache), 2) proxy cached the previous auth result and now sees stale mapping after some pods switch to new key. we need repro steps.

jill_support: repro steps i gave the customer: 1) rotate api key via Console 2) wait 30s 3) hit endpoint with old key -> sometimes 200, sometimes 403 4) restart pod -> 200 consistently. they reproduced on a small scale.

maya_eng: can we get a log snippet from the proxy showing cache hits? also include request-id header. i want to see if proxy logged something like 'auth-cache hit for token sha256=...'

jill_support: paste from edge-proxy logs (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-17T08:24:47Z] req=rid=abc123 path=/v1/generate auth=token-sha256:8b6f auth-cache=HIT backend=svc-a status=200
[2026-03-17T08:25:03Z] req=rid=abc124 path=/v1/generate auth=token-sha256:8b6f auth-cache=HIT backend=svc-b status=403
[2026-03-17T08:25:18Z] req=rid=abc125 path=/v1/generate auth=token-sha256:7d3c auth-cache=MISS backend=svc-b status=200
```

sam_ops: note 8b6f is probably the old key hash, 7d3c the new one. you can see auth-cache=HIT but result status differs by backend. means cache keying is header-value only but the backend ACL decision differs (old key allowed on some backends, revoked on others).

luke_infra: immediate mitigations: 1) purge auth cache globally (deploy-bot can be used to issue cache-purge command) 2) set auth cache TTL to 0 temporarily, 3) trigger rolling restart to ensure all pods read new secret. long-term: add cache keying on a combination of Authorization header + backend-version or service-instance-id to avoid cross-instance staleness.

deploy-bot: triggered cache-purge (id=purge-1773810001) by request of luke_infra.

jill_support: customer applied purge and confirmed error rate dropped to ~0.1% then to 0 after they restarted their remaining 3 pods.

maya_eng: root cause summary i propose: rotation created a short window where some backends accepted old key and some rejected it due to staggered secret propagation + proxy auth caching keyed solely by token value. the proxy served cached allow/deny decisions across instances causing inconsistent behavior.

sam_ops: additional thing we saw: some of our internal agents (vault-agent sidecars) kept the old key in a kube-projected file for up to 2m due to inotify/splice race. so even after vault committed rewrap, those pods didn't reload until lease refresh. that contributed to the split-state.

katie_csm: customer impact notes: B2B account Acme Billing, 15 min incident window, 3% failed requests spike. they want guidance to avoid future disruptions.

luke_infra: recommended action items for customer: - ensure app gracefully picks new secret (hot-reload or ephemeral token handshake) - implement immediate post-rotation probe that hits each instance and restarts any instance still serving old key - set cache-control on proxy auth decisions or tie cache key to instance id - consider short maintenance window for rotation where you pause traffic or pre-warm new keys on all instances.

maya_eng: internal follow-ups for us: 1) make default edge auth cache key include instance-id or run-id 2) improve vault-agent hot-reload reliability and reduce lease jitter 3) add a console checkbox for "graceful rotation" that triggers a rolling restart across pods after rewrap.

jill_support: i'll send the customer a write-up with repro, mitigations, and our planned infra changes. thanks everyone. :heart
